lecture_beats.subject: Operators, basis matrix elements, components, completeness, and operator products
Hermitian operators, eigenvectors, the spectral theorem, rotations, and diagonal form
Five measurement postulates and distinctions among states, observables, eigenvectors, and outcomes
Function-space states, inner products, the position operator, and domain assumptions
Position eigenvalue equation, delta functions, continuous spectra, and generalized normalization
Delta sampling, the wave function as a position component, and the position Born density
Differentiation, anti-Hermiticity, and the integration-by-parts proof for the wave-number operator
Plane-wave eigenfunctions, constant modulus, and generalized continuous eigenstates
Wavelength and the provisional de Broglie identification p equals hbar k
Incompatible position and momentum bases, uncertainty, and the classical wave-packet limit
Complex plane wave visualized as phase winding along a helix
Deferred collapse, momentum probabilities, time evolution, and classical motion

resolved_source_issues.issue: The first spoken Hermitian matrix-element formula is garbled.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The standard adjoint relation is reconstructed and checked against the later expectation-value discussion.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The classroom shorthand could imply that general complex operators have no eigenvectors and that finite rotations are anti-Hermitian.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter distinguishes existence of at least one eigenvector from a complete eigenbasis, identifies finite rotations as unitary, and assigns anti-Hermiticity to the infinitesimal generator.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The unit-area delta approximation could be mistaken for a normalized Hilbert-space state.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter separates unit area from divergent squared norm and states continuous delta normalization explicitly.

resolved_source_issues.issue: Probability at one exact position is imprecise for a continuous spectrum.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter identifies the absolute square as a density and integrates it over intervals.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The spoken anti-Hermitian definition and sign choice are garbled.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter uses the standard adjoint relation and proves Hermiticity of minus i d by dx with its boundary term and operator domain visible.

resolved_source_issues.issue: Plane waves do not decay although decay was used in the integration-by-parts argument.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: Plane waves are treated as generalized eigenstates, with wave-packet, box, and delta-normalization routes stated.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The source video is limited to 320 by 240 pixels.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: Frames are retained as timestamped evidence while equations and diagrams are independently typeset.

uncertain_sources.note: The first Hermitian formula is reconstructed from standard mathematics and later audible statements.
The anti-Hermitian formula lacks a clear spoken complex-conjugation marker; the standard relation is used.
